BiblicalUsage: Karmiyl is carmine — a deep red, the crimson of the temple. Solomon asks Hiram for a man cunning to work in gold and silver and brass, in purple and crimson and blue; and the veil of the temple was made of blue and purple and crimson and fine linen, with cherubim wrought upon it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the crimson in the veil is no accident: the colour of blood hangs between the holy and the most holy, and the way in is through the blood — and that is why the veil tore when the blood was shed. The way in was always through the blood, and the torn veil proves it.
